The video drew condemnation from countries whose citizens were onboard the boats, including the UK, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, and Ireland. **Mike Huckabee**, the US ambassador to Israel, called Ben-Gvir’s behavior “despicable,” while **Giorgia Meloni**, Italy’s prime minister, demanded the release of all Italian citizens involved and an apology for the mistreatment.  **Winston Peters**, New Zealand's foreign affairs minister, condemned Ben-Gvir’s actions and placed a travel ban on him in 2025. The activists were detained after their boats were intercepted while attempting to break the Israeli blockade of Gaza. Rights groups documented widespread abuse and torture of Palestinians by Israeli authorities during the recent conflict.

recent_articles.title: IHC issues notices on applications seeking early hearing of Imaan, Hadi's sentence suspension pleas - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Islamabad High Court** issued notices on multiple applications seeking early hearing of sentence suspension pleas filed by human rights lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chatha in the social media posts case.  **Justice Muhammad Azam Khan** stated that the matter could not be fixed on Monday due to Eidul Azha, but would be scheduled for the first working day after Eid. The **Supreme Court** had directed the IHC to decide within two weeks on their pleas seeking sentence suspension.

recent_articles.title: Bihar cabinet approves ₹10.40 cr VGF to operate direct flight between Gaya Ji-Bangkok - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bihar** cabinet approved ₹10.40 crore in Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to support direct flights between Gaya Ji and Bangkok, with **Indigo Airlines** selected to operate the service. The decision aims to boost international air connectivity and attract religious tourism from Thailand.  The VGF will be provided for up to 12 months, with the airline initially operating two flights weekly. The cabinet also approved funding for healthcare infrastructure development, an industrial reservoir project, and border security enhancements.

recent_articles.title: Australia news live: Penny Wong rebukes Israel over ‘shocking and unacceptable’ treatment of flotilla activists | Australia news | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Penny Wong**, Australia's foreign affairs minister, condemned the actions of **Itamar Ben-Gvir**, Israel’s far-right national security minister, who posted a video of himself abusing bound activists captured during an aid flotilla to Gaza.  Wong joined international condemnation of the footage and called for the release of the detained Australians and for Israel to ensure no ill treatment of any detainees. The Australian Bureau of Statistics will release its latest figures on the country’s jobless rate today, which could impact future Reserve Bank decisions regarding interest rates.

recent_articles.title: How IRGC’s ‘permit’ threats may impact submarine cables in Hormuz? - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps** (IRGC) in **Iran** threatened to impose "permits" on submarine fiber-optic cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz.  Experts warn that while disruptions are possible, they would likely be limited as other connectivity options exist for countries using these cables. The IRGC's threat could disrupt data flow between Asia and Europe, particularly affecting **Qatar**, which hosts a key terminal for the AAE-1 cable. Experts also highlight potential risks to repair vessels due to Iran's military capabilities and territorial claims over the Strait of Hormuz.  However, international law experts argue that Iran lacks legal grounds to demand tolls or permits from passing cables as they fall under UNCLOS regulations.

recent_articles.title: US condemns Israel’s Ben-Gvir while sanctioning Gaza flotilla organisers | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee** joined global criticism of **Israel’s national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir**, after he posted a video taunting detained activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla.  Huckabee condemned Ben-Gvir's actions, but his statement came a day after the US Department of the Treasury sanctioned the flotilla organizers. Critics argue that this double standard reflects a US policy that has long fostered impunity for **Israel** and emboldened its far-right figures. The latest sanctions target four organizers of the Global Sumud Flotilla, which seeks to break the blockade of Gaza and deliver aid.  The Trump administration's stance on Israel remains consistent despite condemnation from other countries and human rights groups.

recent_articles.title: Russian jets intercepting an RAF spy plane is 'serious incident'
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Defence** stated that two **Russian Su-35** and **Su-27** jets "dangerously" intercepted an unarmed **RAF Rivet Joint** surveillance aircraft over the Black Sea last month. The incident, which occurred while the aircraft was conducting a routine international flight to support NATO's eastern flank, has been described as "really serious" by **BBC Security Correspondent Frank Gardner**, who highlighted the potential for escalation due to existing tensions between Russia and NATO.

recent_articles.title: Could a football match soften North Korea-South Korea relations?
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Naegohyang**, the North Korean women's football team, advanced to the Asian Women's Champions League final after defeating **South Korea's Suwon** in a semi-final match. The victory marks the first time athletes from North Korea have crossed the border since 2018 and drew significant interest with over 7,000 tickets selling out within hours.  The outcome has sparked questions about whether this rare sporting event could contribute to thawing diplomatic relations between **North Korea** and **South Korea**.

recent_articles.title: US indicts Cuba’s former leader Raul Castro: Why it matters | Raul Castro News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **United States** has indicted former Cuban leader Raul Castro on charges of conspiracy to kill US nationals, murder, and aircraft destruction. The indictment stems from the 1996 shooting down of two planes operated by a Cuban exile group, Brothers to the Rescue, killing four Americans. This move follows a pattern of US criminal cases targeting foreign leaders, including Venezuela's **Nicolas Maduro**, and comes amid escalating tensions between Cuba and the US.  The Trump administration has imposed sanctions on Cuba and threatened military action if its demands for regime change are not met. However, some analysts believe the indictment is part of a broader strategy to pressure Cuba's government through economic reforms rather than regime change.

recent_articles.title: British Council staff in Italy to strike over proposed 80% workforce cut | Foreign policy | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The British Council**, a leading institution of soft power founded in 1934, is facing financial difficulties due to a £197m government loan from the UK government.  Staff at its offices in Italy are protesting over proposed cuts that would eliminate 80% of its workforce, impacting teaching activities across Rome, Milan, and Naples. The organization's chief executive, Scott McDonald, has warned that without government intervention, the **British Council** could disappear within a decade, harming the UK’s global status.  The **CGIL**, the Italian General Confederation of Labour, accuses the **British Council** of masking a political decision by blaming it for an alleged corporate crisis.

recent_articles.title: Will Raúl Castro’s indictment over 1996 shooting down of civilian planes push US and Cuba closer to war? - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The indictment of **Raúl Castro** by the US for his role in the 1996 shooting down of civilian planes has heightened tensions between Washington and Havana.  **Donald Trump**, US president, has criticized Cuba's government while suggesting he is open to a deal. **Marco Rubio**, secretary of state, supports removing Cuba’s current leadership from power. Cuban President **Miguel Díaz-Canel** has responded defiantly, accusing the US of attempting to force political change on Cuba.  Analysts warn that isolating Cuba’s leadership could make the situation more volatile and potentially lead to a military confrontation.

recent_articles.title: No double standards, we condemn Russia, U.S. and Israel for international law violations: Norway’s Foreign Minister - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Espen Barth Eide**, **Norwegian Foreign Minister**, urged **India** and **Norway** to increase their engagement to avoid becoming overly reliant on any single global power.  He highlighted the potential for increased trade, technology transfer, and renewable energy cooperation as key areas of focus. While Norway prefers India reduce its reliance on Russian oil, it acknowledges India's concerns regarding energy security.

recent_articles.title: WHO says Ebola risk high regionally, low worldwide - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **World Health Organisation (WHO)** declared a public health emergency of international concern for the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, but not a pandemic.  **Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus**, WHO chief, stated that while investigations into the outbreak's origins are ongoing, it likely began two months ago and the scale of the situation in eastern DRC is much larger than confirmed cases. **Lucille Blumberg**, chair of the WHO emergency committee, said the current situation does not meet the criteria for a pandemic emergency.  **Marco Rubio**, US Secretary of State, criticized the WHO's response to the outbreak as being "a little late".

recent_articles.title: What’s the significance of the Russian president’s visit to China? | International Trade News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vladimir Putin** visited **China**, meeting with **Xi Jinping** to strengthen ties between the two nations.  The visit comes a week after **Donald Trump**'s trip to Beijing, highlighting the strength of their partnership. The leaders emphasized their shared opposition to US actions and policies, including the war against Iran and global tariffs. They discussed a potential multipolar world order where the United States does not hold dominance.

recent_articles.title: Austrian ex-intelligence officer found guilty of Russia spying charges
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Egisto Ott**, a former Austrian intelligence officer, has been found guilty of spying for Russia and other charges. A jury in Vienna sentenced him to four years and one month in prison after finding him guilty of providing information to Russian intelligence officers and fugitive executive **Jan Marsalek**.  The case has raised concerns about the potential for continued Russian espionage activity within Austria. Prosecutors allege that Ott, who denies the charges, received payment from **Marsalek** for his actions. The investigation into **Marsalek**, also an Austrian citizen wanted by German authorities, is ongoing.

recent_articles.title: 'There won’t be escalation': Donald Trump reacts to Raúl Castro DOJ indictment over 1996 civilian plane shootdown - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** downplayed fears of escalating tensions with **Cuba** following the indictment of former president **Raúl Castro** for his role in the 1996 shooting down of civilian aircraft. **Todd Blanche**, acting Attorney General, announced the charges against **Castro** and five others, accusing him of conspiracy to kill US nationals and related offenses.  The incident, which saw two small planes destroyed by Cuban fighter jets, has long been a point of contention between the two countries. **Díaz-Canel**, the current Cuban president, has rejected accusations from the US while **Trump** maintains his focus on expanding influence in the Western Hemisphere.

recent_articles.title: US charges former Cuban president Raúl Castro over 1996 downing of planes
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The United States has charged former Cuban leader Raúl Castro with conspiracy to kill US nationals and other crimes over the downing of two planes in 1996. The charges, revived from a 2003 case, accuse Castro and five others of shooting down an aircraft belonging to Brothers to the Rescue and killing four people, including three Americans. **President Miguel Díaz-Canel** of **Cuba** called the charges "a political manoeuvre, devoid of any legal foundation" while **Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche** stated that the US would also charge Castro with destruction of aircraft and murder counts.  The move comes amidst increased US pressure on Cuba's communist rule.
